drhp.business: Quicktouch is a diversified technology holding company operating through wholly owned and majority-owned subsidiaries across Edutech/ERP (QuickCampus brand), AI & Robotics Labs for schools (Techquench), and exploring electronics/IT hardware trading and permissible fintech activities. Its proposed Payment Aggregator business did not receive final RBI authorisation during the year, and the Company also pursues acquisition-led growth including revival of distressed businesses via the CIRP route.
drhp.end_markets: Educational institutions (India)|Electronics and IT hardware trading (proposed)|Fintech / digital financial services (proposed)
drhp.expansion: Quicktouch's expansion is subsidiary-led rather than a physical capex programme: Techquench (AI & Robotics Labs) is expanding into educational institutions; the Edutech/ERP business (QuickCampus) is being scaled through Quickcampus Private Limited; and the Company is evaluating electronics/IT hardware trading, permissible fintech activities, and further acquisition/revival opportunities (including via the CIRP route) as new growth avenues. The proposed Payment Aggregator business did not receive final RBI authorisation during the year.

risks.note: The Company is exploring fintech and other regulated activities; changes in laws, licensing requirements or regulatory policy may impact its ability to enter or expand such businesses. The RBI's rejection of the proposed Payment Aggregator authorisation during FY2025-26 illustrates this risk.

The Company is entering new, unproven business areas (electronics/IT hardware trading, alternative fintech) that may require significant investment, specialised expertise and time to reach scale and profitability.

Growing dependence on technology, digital platforms, software and data exposes the Company to cyberattacks, data breaches, system failures and technology obsolescence that could affect operations and reputation.

The Edutech, technology, electronics and fintech sectors are highly competitive, with established and new technology-driven entrants that may pressure pricing, margins, customer acquisition and market share.
The Company's strategy includes acquisitions and revival of businesses via the CIRP route; delays in integration, restructuring or achieving expected synergies may affect anticipated returns.
Financial performance may be affected by fluctuations in revenue, operating costs, working-capital requirements and fund availability.
Growth in technology, AI, Robotics and fintech-related businesses requires skilled professionals; retention and availability of appropriately skilled manpower may constrain execution of growth plans.

Changes in economic conditions, consumer demand, interest rates, supply-chain conditions and market sentiment may affect existing and proposed businesses, particularly the proposed electronics and IT hardware trading business.
